What Derivatives Tell Us About the Shape of a Graph

Increasing/decreasing, local max/min, concave up/down and inflection points, all read from f′ and f″.

0 / 10 problems mastered

This section turns signs into shape. The sign of f′f'f′ tells you whether the graph goes up or down. The sign of f′′f''f′′ tells you whether it bends like a cup or a cap. Almost every homework problem (#1–29 and #45–65) is the same routine: find where f′f'f′ or f′′f''f′′ is zero, then test the sign on each interval.

Increasing/Decreasing Test

f′>0f'>0f′>0 on an interval ⇒ fff increasing there. f′<0f'<0f′<0 ⇒ decreasing.

First Derivative Test

At a critical number ccc: f′f'f′ changes +→−+\to-+→− ⇒ local max. −→+-\to+−→+ ⇒ local min. No sign change ⇒ neither.

Concavity Test

f′′>0f''>0f′′>0 ⇒ concave up (cup ∪). f′′<0f''<0f′′<0 ⇒ concave down (cap ∩).

Inflection point

A point on the graph where the concavity changes. Find where f′′=0f''=0f′′=0 or is undefined, then check that the sign of f′′f''f′′ really flips.

Second Derivative Test

If f′(c)=0f'(c)=0f′(c)=0: f′′(c)>0f''(c)>0f′′(c)>0 ⇒ local min. f′′(c)<0f''(c)<0f′′(c)<0 ⇒ local max. f′′(c)=0f''(c)=0f′′(c)=0 ⇒ the test says nothing; use the first derivative test.

The routine (sign chart)

  1. Find f′f'f′ and factor it.
  2. Critical numbers: where f′=0f'=0f′=0 or f′f'f′ is undefined (inside the domain).
  3. Cut the number line at those points. Pick a test value in each piece and record the sign of f′f'f′.
  4. Read off increasing/decreasing and the local max/min. Plug the xxx back into fff to get the values.
  5. Repeat steps 1–3 with f′′f''f′′ for concavity and inflection points.

Answer in the form the question asks: intervals for “where increasing”, values f(c)f(c)f(c) for “local maximum value”, and points (x,y)(x,y)(x,y) for “inflection points”.

Worked examples

Full analysis of a cubic

f(x)=2x3−3x2−12xf(x)=2x^3-3x^2-12xf(x)=2x3−3x2−12x.

  1. f′(x)=6x2−6x−12=6(x−2)(x+1)f'(x)=6x^2-6x-12=6(x-2)(x+1)f′(x)=6x2−6x−12=6(x−2)(x+1), so the critical numbers are −1-1−1 and 222.
  2. Signs of f′f'f′: +++ on (−∞,−1)(-\infty,-1)(−∞,−1), −-− on (−1,2)(-1,2)(−1,2), +++ on (2,∞)(2,\infty)(2,∞).
  3. Local max f(−1)=7f(-1)=7f(−1)=7; local min f(2)=−20f(2)=-20f(2)=−20.
  4. f′′(x)=12x−6=0f''(x)=12x-6=0f′′(x)=12x−6=0 at x=12x=\tfrac12x=21​: concave down before it, concave up after it.

Inflection point (12,−132)(\tfrac12,-\tfrac{13}{2})(21​,−213​)

Second derivative test

f(x)=x5−5x+3f(x)=x^5-5x+3f(x)=x5−5x+3. f′(x)=5x4−5=0⇒x=±1f'(x)=5x^4-5=0\Rightarrow x=\pm1f′(x)=5x4−5=0⇒x=±1. f′′(x)=20x3f''(x)=20x^3f′′(x)=20x3: f′′(1)=20>0f''(1)=20>0f′′(1)=20>0 gives a min, and f′′(−1)=−20<0f''(-1)=-20<0f′′(−1)=−20<0 gives a max.

Local max f(−1)=7f(-1)=7f(−1)=7; local min f(1)=−1f(1)=-1f(1)=−1

Traps

Giving \(x\) instead of the value

“Find the local maximum value” wants f(c)f(c)f(c), not ccc. Say “local max f(−1)=7f(-1)=7f(−1)=7”.

\(f''=0\) doesn't guarantee an inflection point

f(x)=x4f(x)=x^4f(x)=x4 has f′′(0)=0f''(0)=0f′′(0)=0, but it is concave up on both sides. Always check that the sign flips.

Second Derivative Test gives up when \(f''(c)=0\)

That doesn't mean “neither”. Fall back on the First Derivative Test.

Forgetting where \(f'\) is undefined

x1/3x^{1/3}x1/3 and x2/3x^{2/3}x2/3 produce critical numbers where f′f'f′ blows up (like x=0x=0x=0 in #8).
